subtitle: Some disabilities and access needs are not apparent to others. This course helps you respond respectfully to the work barriers employees face in those situations.
scope: For DHS supervisors supporting staff and responding to possible accommodation needs. This course does not diagnose a condition, determine an individual’s legal eligibility, approve an accommodation or adjudicate performance and conduct cases. Use the actual agency accommodation, HR and safety processes.
introTranscript: A disability is not always visible, and a work barrier may not look the way a supervisor expects. An employee may need a different method, an adjustment or a private conversation without being able or willing to explain health details to the team. This course follows practice DHS situations involving concentration, fatigue, communication and changing work demands. These examples do not establish a diagnosis or legal outcome. You will separate observations from assumptions, recognize a request in ordinary words, discuss the task, protect confidentiality and follow the proper process through implementation. The goal is a respectful response that supports the work without asking a supervisor to act as a clinician.

lessons.title: Notice the work barrier without diagnosing the person
lessons.summary: An appearance, communication style or isolated result cannot establish a disability, effort or the cause of a work problem.
lessons.objective: Separate an observable work fact from a judgment about health or effort.
objectives: Separate an observable work fact from a judgment about health or effort.
Explain why a non-apparent or episodic condition cannot be assessed from appearance alone.
Prepare a private work conversation that does not presume a diagnosis.
takeaways: Visibility does not determine whether a disability or barrier exists.
A work observation is a starting point for inquiry, not a diagnosis.
Keep the conversation on the task and appropriate support route.
lessons.statement: You do not need to recognize a diagnosis to respond respectfully to a work barrier.

image.caption: A private conversation can focus on the task without asking the employee to prove a condition by appearance.

intro.heading: Replace an assumption with a useful question
intro.body:
A practice DHS supervisor notices that an analyst loses track of instructions during rapid meetings but produces careful written analysis afterward. The supervisor calls the analyst inattentive. The observations do not establish that conclusion. The meeting’s pace, information format, work conditions or other factors may matter. A supervisor should discuss the actual work requirement and observed difficulty rather than diagnose a condition or infer motivation.

Non-apparent disability describes a disability that is not readily visible to others. It is not a separate legal eligibility test or a list of behaviors supervisors can use to identify people. A person can appear comfortable in one situation and encounter a substantial barrier in another. Current ADA regulations also address conditions that are episodic or in remission: they can be disabilities if they would substantially limit a major life activity when active. That does not authorize a supervisor to decide an individual case from a brief example.

Avoid forcing a choice between a health explanation and a judgment about effort. You can say, “The task requires us to capture the decision accurately. I noticed the spoken sequence was difficult to follow. What work information or method would help?” The employee may describe a task issue, request a disability-related adjustment or choose not to share health details. Each response needs its proper handling; the supervisor should not invent a diagnosis to explain silence.

Observe performance with relevant facts and standards. An unfamiliar communication style or one hard meeting is not proof that a person cannot do the job. Nor does a request automatically eliminate the job’s actual requirements. Appropriate accommodation, HR and technical processes help examine those different questions.

For this lesson’s exercise, use practice observations. Write what was required, what happened and what remains unknown. This keeps the inquiry concrete and creates room for a respectful response without turning the supervisor into a clinician.

lessons.keyStatement: Describe what happened in the work; do not convert it into a medical or character verdict.

flashcards.back: A disability not readily visible to others. The phrase does not determine an individual’s legal eligibility or supply a diagnostic checklist for supervisors.
A specific work event that can be described, such as a missed spoken step. It does not by itself establish the cause, motive or health condition.
A condition that may vary in activity. Current regulations recognize that such a condition can qualify if substantially limiting when active; actual application needs the proper process.
A discussion focused on relevant duties, barriers and support routes, without requiring the employee to explain medical history to the supervisor or group.

items.title: What is the actual observation?
items.body: “The final spoken instruction was missed” is different from “the employee does not care.” Record the task and relevant result. A specific observation can support inquiry while a character label can shut it down before the facts are understood.

items.title: What remains unknown?
items.body: The reason for a difficulty may not be visible. Do not assign a diagnosis, disability status or intention from a style, appearance or rumor. Acknowledge uncertainty and use appropriate work and accommodation processes.

items.title: What can you ask usefully?
items.body: Clarify the required outcome and practical barrier. Let the employee raise a request without imposing special terminology. Medical documentation and individual eligibility questions belong with the proper roles, not a supervisor’s informal test.

tabs.label: Observation
tabs.body: “The analyst asked for the decision in writing after the rapid discussion.” This describes an event. It does not say why the request was made or whether a disability exists.

tabs.label: Assumption
tabs.body: “The analyst is not committed because they need written information.” This assigns motive without evidence and confuses a method preference or need with effort.

tabs.label: Useful response
tabs.body: “Let’s make sure the decision and next action are clear. Is there a work barrier or adjustment you want to discuss through the appropriate process?” This invites a practical response without diagnosing.

check.question: An employee looks comfortable during one task but reports a barrier in another. What can the supervisor conclude?
check.correct: Appearance in one situation does not settle the reported barrier or disability question; discuss the task and use the appropriate process.
wrong: The employee cannot have a disability because they looked comfortable earlier.
The supervisor should diagnose the condition from the report.
The request proves that every performance expectation must be removed.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. Different tasks and conditions can produce different experiences. The specific need deserves a proper response without an unsupported medical or performance verdict.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Do not use appearance as proof of absence, assign a diagnosis or infer that a request erases all duties. Keep the actual task and process distinct.

items.text: The spoken instruction changed twice during the meeting.
What work information would help you complete this task?
You looked well yesterday, so the barrier cannot be real.
The analyst requested the final decision in writing.
Would you like information about the appropriate adjustment process?
This communication style proves a particular diagnosis.

lessons.next: Next, recognize an accommodation request without requiring a special label or public disclosure.

scenario.context: In this example, a supervisor hears that an employee needs fewer interruptions to complete a review. The supervisor says the employee cannot need support because their condition is not visible.
options: Retain that conclusion because appearance is decisive.
Discuss the actual work barrier privately, recognize any disability-related request and use the appropriate process without deciding from appearance.
Ask coworkers to identify the employee’s diagnosis.
responses: Visibility is not the legal or practical test. The reported task barrier remains to be considered.
This responds to the work and preserves the proper decision route. It does not promise a specific adjustment or diagnose the employee.
Coworker speculation is not an appropriate medical or accommodation process. Protect confidentiality.

lessons.transfer: Rewrite a practice judgment about effort as a task observation, an acknowledged uncertainty and a respectful private question.

move.control: You can replace assumptions with relevant work facts.
move.failure: Appearance or style becomes a verdict about health and effort.
move.next: Describe the barrier and offer the proper process without trying to diagnose it.

lessons.title: Recognize a request in ordinary words
lessons.summary: A person may ask for a disability-related adjustment without a form, a diagnosis in the conversation or legal terminology.
lessons.objective: Recognize ordinary-language communications that may initiate an accommodation request.
objectives: Recognize ordinary-language communications that may initiate an accommodation request.
Explain the supervisor’s prompt forwarding and communication role under MMB Policy 1433.
Distinguish a general work preference from a request needing further respectful clarification.
takeaways: Requests can be oral, written or otherwise communicated.
Special terms and a completed form are not prerequisites to recognizing the request.
Clarify the work need and forward through the actual process.
lessons.statement: A request should not fail because the person did not use the agency’s vocabulary.

image.caption: The first response can acknowledge the need and identify a clear next step.

intro.heading: Do not turn the first exchange into a language test
intro.body:
A DHS employee says, “Because of a health condition, I need a quieter way to complete the detailed review.” The supervisor replies that only a formal written ADA request counts. MMB Policy 1433 does not support that response. Requests can be communicated in ordinary language through different methods. The person does not have to use a particular legal phrase for the supervisor to recognize and route a possible request.

Not every preference is an accommodation request. A person might simply prefer a different method, or they may be identifying a disability-related barrier without knowing how to describe it. Clarify respectfully when needed: explain the work discussion and available process rather than asking for a diagnosis or imposing a required script. Do not use ambiguity as a reason to ignore a stated disability-related need.

The supervisor’s next step is prompt handling through the policy and agency procedure. Forward the request to the appropriate decision-maker or coordinator and tell the employee who will handle it. A referral should not feel like a dismissal. Explain what the supervisor will do with the relevant work information and how the person can receive the next process communication. Do not invent a contact or promise a universal decision deadline.

A helpful first response might be: “Thank you for raising the work barrier. I will connect this with the appropriate accommodation process. We can identify the relevant task and what is difficult, while the coordinator handles any documentation question.” It respects the person without deciding eligibility or approving the requested option in advance.

During this exchange, maintain the confidentiality boundaries and use appropriate records. An informal conversation in a team meeting may need to move to a private setting. The person should not have to describe medical details publicly to obtain the right route. The course’s practice is about recognizing and responding; formal decisions stay with the authorized process.

inThisLesson: Forward promptly and explain the next role.
Avoid public disclosure and premature decisions.
lessons.keyStatement: Acknowledge the need, discuss the relevant work and connect the real process.

flashcards.back: A communication asking for a disability-related work change without prescribed legal words. Respond through the policy rather than grading the wording.
A respectful effort to understand the work need and which process fits. It is not a supervisor’s medical interview or a demand for a particular script.
Forwarding through the actual accommodation process without unnecessary delay, while telling the person who will handle the decision.
A clear response showing that the request was heard. It does not itself establish eligibility or approve a particular accommodation.

items.title: Say what you will do
items.body: A vague “talk to someone” can leave the person uncertain whether the request is being handled. Explain the actual next route and the supervisor’s work-information role. Use the agency process and real contact rather than inventing a separate pathway.

items.title: Keep the door open
items.body: If the request is unclear, explain the available process and invite a practical clarification. Do not assume the person understands legal labels or has already researched the procedure. Ordinary language can still communicate a genuine need.

items.title: Avoid a premature answer
items.body: Neither automatic approval nor immediate rejection substitutes for the process. Acknowledge the request and route the actual facts. A preferred tool or method can be considered without a supervisor promising an outcome beyond their authority.

tabs.label: Explicit connection
tabs.body: The employee connects a requested change to a health condition or disability. Recognize the possible accommodation request and forward promptly through the policy. Do not demand special words.

tabs.label: Unclear connection
tabs.body: The employee describes a barrier without explaining whether a disability-related adjustment is requested. Clarify respectfully and explain the route, keeping medical inquiry limits in view.

tabs.label: Public conversation
tabs.body: The need is raised in front of the team. Acknowledge it without asking for details there, and move the personal process to the appropriate private channel. The group can discuss shared task improvements separately.

check.question: An employee asks orally for a work adjustment because of a condition but has not completed a form. What should the supervisor do?
check.correct: Recognize the possible request and handle it promptly through the actual process, explaining the next responsible role.
wrong: Ignore it until the employee uses the exact term reasonable accommodation.
Require the employee to disclose medical details at the team meeting.
Promise automatic approval of the specific requested option.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The policy recognizes different communication methods and ordinary language. The form may support the process, but its absence is not a reason to ignore the request.
check.feedbackIncorrect: An exact legal term or completed form is not a gate to recognizing a request made in ordinary words; the initial request should not be ignored. Recognition is also not automatic approval of the particular option. A team meeting is not an appropriate setting for demanding medical disclosure. Respond promptly through the actual process, explain the next responsible role and preserve information limits.

items.text: I will forward this through our accommodation process and identify the next role.
Can we clarify the required task and the work barrier?
Nothing counts until you use the exact legal phrase.
Let’s continue the personal process privately rather than in the group.
Here is the appropriate process if you are requesting a disability-related change.
Tell all coworkers your diagnosis before we discuss the task.

lessons.next: Next, discuss the actual duty without collecting accommodation medical documentation.

scenario.context: In this example, an employee raises a need during a team meeting. The supervisor asks them to explain their full condition in front of coworkers so the group can decide whether it is reasonable.
options: Move the individual discussion to the proper private process, recognize the request and keep the group’s role focused on work arrangements.
Continue because group agreement is required for medical eligibility.
Ignore the request to avoid any private conversation.
responses: This protects confidentiality and authority. The group does not need medical details or decide the individual request.
The accommodation process does not delegate eligibility to a coworker vote.
Avoidance does not provide the prompt appropriate response. Acknowledge and route the need.

lessons.transfer: Draft a practice first response acknowledging an ordinary-language request, identifying the next role and preserving confidentiality without promising the decision.

move.control: You can recognize and connect the process early.
move.failure: Forms, vocabulary or public disclosure become prerequisites to being heard.
move.next: Respond promptly in ordinary language and explain the actual next route.

lessons.title: Discuss the duty, not the medical history
lessons.summary: Supervisors need relevant work information. Appropriate documentation and formal assessment questions belong to authorized roles.
lessons.objective: Distinguish a relevant duty discussion from an accommodation medical-documentation request.
objectives: Distinguish a relevant duty discussion from an accommodation medical-documentation request.
Explain why a customary method is not automatically an essential function.
Identify a medical, safety or legal question requiring appropriate specialist handling.
takeaways: Describe the necessary work result and actual barrier.
MMB Policy 1433 bars supervisor requests for accommodation medical documentation.
Formal medical and safety questions need proper authority and evidence.
lessons.statement: A practical task discussion can be detailed without becoming a medical investigation.

image.caption: The work requirement gives the conversation a focus while the coordinator handles appropriate documentation.

intro.heading: Keep the roles distinct
intro.body:
A practice DHS analyst requests fewer interruptions while completing complex reviews. The supervisor wants to know how the review is performed and which interruptions interfere. Those are useful work questions. Asking for the analyst’s full medical file is a different matter. Under MMB Policy 1433, supervisors and managers must not request medical information or documentation for accommodation; the ADA Coordinator handles appropriate documentation questions.

Identify the actual duty and required result. Is uninterrupted time necessary for a portion of the review, or must the employee respond to a real-time service function? A customary way of scheduling work is not automatically an essential function. Current ADA regulations distinguish fundamental job duties from marginal functions and identify several forms of evidence. The responsible process examines the actual job rather than treating the manager’s preferred method as the entire legal analysis.

The employee can help explain the barrier and possible work methods without disclosing an entire health history. If disability or need is not apparent and relevant documentation may be needed, that question belongs to the coordinator under the policy. Documentation should be appropriate to the question, not an automatic demand for unrelated records. Do not invent local medical-review steps or collect evidence in a personal supervisor folder.

Employment medical inquiries outside the accommodation-documentation context also have legal limits. EEOC guidance discusses job-relatedness, business necessity and specific circumstances. A supervisor should not generalize those conditions into permission to interrogate staff based on rumors. Involve appropriate HR, ADA, safety or legal roles for an actual concern, and follow immediate emergency procedures when necessary.

For a practice exercise, write the duty, expected result, observed barrier and specialist question separately. The distinction helps the supervisor contribute knowledge of the work while preserving the correct boundaries. It does not decide an actual employee’s diagnosis, legal eligibility, fitness or essential-function dispute.

inThisLesson: Describe the real duty and work result.
lessons.keyStatement: Contribute the work facts; do not substitute a supervisor’s medical file or diagnosis for the proper process.

flashcards.back: A fundamental duty under the applicable definition and actual job evidence. It is not automatically every preferred method or customary procedure.
What prevents effective performance or participation in the relevant task. It can be discussed without requesting a complete medical history.
MMB Policy 1433 keeps accommodation medical-documentation requests with the appropriate coordinator rather than supervisors and managers.
A medical, safety or legal issue requiring the authorized process and appropriate evidence. A course scenario cannot adjudicate it.

accordion.heading: Ask with a clear work purpose

items.title: Clarify the required outcome
items.body: Identify what must be completed, its quality and relevant timing. Distinguish a genuine service requirement from a habitual meeting or scheduling choice. Accurate work facts help the coordinator consider options without changing actual duties informally.

items.title: Describe the barrier precisely
items.body: Ask which task conditions interfere and what the employee proposes. Avoid requests for medications, diagnostic history or unrelated records. The coordinator determines appropriate documentation questions under the policy.

items.title: Use the right specialist
items.body: A safety concern needs the actual facts and the appropriate authority. A rumor or diagnosis label does not establish a threat. Keep immediate emergency response distinct from formal employment or medical assessment.

tabs.label: Work question
tabs.body: “Which part of the review requires sustained attention, and what output must be completed?” This can clarify the task without a medical inquiry.

tabs.label: Improper supervisor documentation request
tabs.body: “Send me your complete medical file so I can decide the accommodation.” This crosses the policy’s documentation boundary and is not repaired by a promise to keep it private.

tabs.label: Appropriate referral
tabs.body: “I will provide the work facts to the proper process, and the coordinator will handle documentation questions.” This preserves the supervisor’s contribution and the specialist role.

check.question: A supervisor needs to understand an accommodation request. Which action fits MMB Policy 1433?
check.correct: Discuss relevant duties and barriers while leaving accommodation medical-documentation requests to the ADA Coordinator.
wrong: Collect all medical records in the supervisor’s personal folder.
Treat every customary method as a legally essential function without examining the job.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The supervisor’s task knowledge is useful within the boundary. The appropriate process handles documentation and formal conclusions.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Privacy promises do not expand authority. Use actual work evidence and proper roles rather than a medical collection, a method shortcut or rumor.

sorting.heading: Which role does the action fit?

items.text: Describe the required report result and relevant deadline.
Determine what appropriate medical documentation is needed.
Ask the employee to send their full medical record directly to the supervisor.
Explain which interruptions are part of a genuine service duty.
Assess a specific formal safety question through authorized roles.
Ask coworkers to diagnose the employee.

lessons.next: Next, compare effective work options without making one condition label a recipe for every person.

scenario.context: In this example, a manager insists that reviewing information only during rapid spoken meetings is an essential function because the team has always worked that way. The analyst proposes another method of receiving the same required information.
options: Reject the option because custom equals essential function.
Examine the actual duties, evidence and required outcome through the appropriate process, rather than treating the customary method as decisive.
Remove all duties before any discussion.
responses: Habit alone is not the full essential-function analysis. The actual work and proper authority matter.
This preserves the work purpose while allowing appropriate consideration of a different method. It does not promise approval or decide the legal question in the course.
A request does not automatically eliminate the job’s duties. Clarify the result and consider effective options through the process.

lessons.transfer: Prepare a practice task note with duty, required result, barrier and question for the coordinator, without medical-history content.

move.control: You can supply accurate work knowledge.
move.failure: The supervisor becomes a clinician or treats a habit as the whole legal test.
move.next: Keep work facts detailed and medical or formal assessment questions in their proper route.

lessons.title: Compare options for this person and this task
lessons.summary: A condition label does not prescribe one adjustment. Effectiveness, preference and the actual work need appropriate consideration.
lessons.objective: Compare proposed options by the barrier and relevant task outcome.
objectives: Compare proposed options by the barrier and relevant task outcome.
Explain why shared supports do not automatically replace an individual accommodation.
Recognize when effectiveness, hardship or a denial question needs the authorized process.
takeaways: Consider the individual and actual task, not a stereotype.
Take the person’s preference seriously through the process.
Shared improvements and individual decisions are related but distinct.
lessons.statement: An effective option is not whichever is easiest to describe or familiar to the team. It must address the relevant work barrier.

image.caption: Options should be compared for their task effect without assuming the same solution fits everyone.

intro.heading: Use the barrier as the comparison point
intro.body:
The practice DHS analyst suggests a quieter review period and written priority information. The supervisor assumes a generic time-management course will solve the problem because it is easy to arrange. It might support general skills, but it is not automatically an effective response to the particular disability-related barrier. Examine the actual task and proposed options through the accommodation process.

The person’s experience and preference matter. Under the policy and EEOC guidance, the interactive process considers effectiveness and appropriate alternatives. An employer may choose among effective accommodations in the applicable circumstances, while considering the employee’s preference; preference alone is not the entire decision, and convenience alone does not establish effectiveness. The authorized roles evaluate the actual options and any formal hardship or denial question.

Do not use a diagnostic label as a universal recipe. Two people with a similarly named condition may encounter different barriers or prefer different methods. One employee may need a change in information delivery; another may need an adjustment in the work environment. A learning example describes a possible inquiry, not a clinical recommendation or proof that a particular option must be approved.

Shared practices can reduce barriers: clear agendas, usable documents, maintained tools and predictable task instructions. They may help many staff, but do not automatically close an individual request. Conversely, an individual adjustment does not necessarily repair an inaccessible tool for everyone. Keep the shared owner and individual process connected without merging their decisions.

For a practice comparison, state the barrier, the required result, each option’s likely task effect and what evidence is still needed. Avoid a made-up numerical score implying medical suitability. Record uncertainty and bring the question to the appropriate process. The goal is a supported decision and meaningful work participation, not a fastest-to-close request.

inThisLesson: Keep uncertainty and formal authority visible.
lessons.keyStatement: Compare effectiveness for the actual person and task; do not substitute a label or convenience for evidence.

flashcards.back: An adjustment addressing the relevant barrier and employment purpose in the actual situation. It needs the appropriate process and evidence, not a diagnostic stereotype.
The person’s expressed choice or experience of an option. Take it seriously while the authorized process considers effectiveness and other applicable requirements.
A change to common work practices or tools. It can help the team but does not automatically decide or close an individual accommodation request.
A question not yet answered about an option’s effectiveness or implementation. Keep it visible rather than converting it into a favorable score.

items.title: Start with the task result
items.body: A quieter review period may help concentration, but the actual service duties and scheduling facts still need examination. State the result and constraints accurately so the process can compare options rather than starting from a broad label.

items.title: Listen to the employee’s experience
items.body: An option that appears simple may have a barrier the supervisor has missed. Ask about the relevant effect and let the person correct the summary. Do not treat disagreement as ingratitude or inability.

items.title: Route a formal limit
items.body: Hardship, threat and denial questions need the actual criteria, evidence and authority. A supervisor’s preference or informal budget concern is not a completed legal determination. Use the appropriate consultation and decision process.

tabs.label: General development
tabs.body: Learning or coaching may address a skill need. It should not be presented as a substitute for a disability-related adjustment without examining the actual barrier and appropriate process.

tabs.label: Shared design
tabs.body: Clear written instructions and usable materials can improve the common work environment. Keep an individual request open through its process if it still needs consideration.

tabs.label: Individual accommodation
tabs.body: The authorized process considers an effective adjustment for the person’s situation. It does not automatically determine every shared product repair or waive all job requirements.

check.question: A supervisor offers a general productivity course instead of considering a requested disability-related adjustment. What should be examined?
check.correct: Whether the proposed response addresses the actual barrier and task through the accommodation process, rather than assuming general training is sufficient.
wrong: Whether any course automatically replaces an accommodation.
Whether every employee with a similar condition must receive the same tool.
Whether the easiest option can be declared effective without inquiry.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. Development and accommodation can be related but are different questions. The actual barrier, person’s input and proper process determine the supported response.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Avoid one-size-fits-all or convenience-based answers. Training, tools and work adjustments need to be examined for their actual purpose and effectiveness.

items.text: How does this method support the required review result?
The team maintains clearer written instructions for everyone.
All people with this diagnosis need the same software.
What remaining barrier does the employee identify in the alternative?
A course supports a separately identified skill-development goal.
The easiest option is effective because the supervisor prefers it.

lessons.next: Next, keep confidentiality and actual performance responsibilities clear while the process proceeds.

scenario.context: In this example, an employee explains why a proposed alternative would not address the barrier. The supervisor says they should be grateful for any offer and plans to close the request.
options: Close it because gratitude is the standard.
Discuss the specific concern, document the relevant work information and use the authorized process to consider effectiveness and the appropriate decision.
Publish the employee’s condition so coworkers can judge the choice.
responses: An offer’s effectiveness is not measured by whether the person sounds grateful. The concern needs the proper examination.
This treats the person’s task information as evidence and preserves decision authority. It does not guarantee the preferred option.
Coworker judgment and disclosure are not the accommodation process. Protect confidentiality.

lessons.transfer: Compare two practice options using the barrier, required result, person’s input and unresolved effectiveness question. Avoid invented clinical scores.

move.control: You can prepare a useful comparison.
move.failure: A label, general course or convenient offer replaces individual consideration.
move.next: Bring task evidence and the person’s experience to the authorized decision process.

lessons.title: Preserve confidentiality and fair work expectations
lessons.summary: Coworkers do not need private accommodation reasons. Actual performance or safety concerns require relevant facts and the proper process.
lessons.objective: Respond to coworker questions without disclosing confidential medical or accommodation information.
objectives: Respond to coworker questions without disclosing confidential medical or accommodation information.
Distinguish prospective accommodation from conclusions about past performance.
Identify an actual employment or safety matter that should be routed to authorized roles.
takeaways: Explain work arrangements without revealing private reasons.
A request does not automatically erase past events or decide a performance case.
Use relevant facts and the appropriate employment process.
lessons.statement: The team can understand how work is organized without knowing someone’s medical history.

image.caption: Operational clarity and confidentiality can coexist in a respectful team conversation.

intro.heading: Keep private information and work decisions in the right places
intro.body:
A DHS team notices that an analyst has a different work arrangement. A coworker asks whether the analyst is receiving special treatment. The supervisor considers explaining the condition to defend the arrangement. That would expose private information. Under the accommodation policy and EEOC guidance, medical information and the fact of an accommodation are confidential within the applicable limits. Coworker curiosity is not a reason to disclose it.

Explain the work that colleagues need to coordinate: coverage, response routes or meeting practice, without naming a confidential reason. A useful response is that the agency handles individual work arrangements through appropriate processes and everyone is expected to respect privacy. Do not confirm or deny personal medical information to satisfy a debate about fairness. Formal disclosure questions belong with authorized roles and the applicable rules.

Keep performance and accommodation related but distinct. An employee may request an adjustment after a performance concern has arisen. The request still deserves the appropriate prospective consideration. It does not automatically require erasing earlier performance or conduct findings, and a supervisor should not use the course to decide discipline or an actual legal case. EEOC guidance examines these distinctions; actual agency standards, facts and HR processes matter.

Use observable work evidence rather than stereotypes. A condition label does not prove inability or danger, and a request does not prove bad faith. If there is an immediate emergency, follow the real emergency response. Formal fitness, safety or conduct questions need the appropriate evidence and authorized HR, ADA, safety or legal process.

For the practice exercise, write two separate notes: operational information coworkers need, and confidential process information that stays with the authorized roles. This distinction lets a supervisor maintain clear work expectations without turning a personal request into a public explanation or a shortcut around the proper employment decision.

inThisLesson: Keep prospective requests and past events distinct.
Route formal employment and safety matters.
lessons.keyStatement: Privacy does not prevent clear work coordination; it limits what personal information should be shared.

flashcards.back: Operational information colleagues need to carry out their duties. It is different from a confidential diagnosis or accommodation reason.
Medical information and accommodation information protected under the applicable policy and legal limits. A coworker’s curiosity does not create authority to share it.
Examining an adjustment for work going forward. It does not automatically erase a past event or decide an existing performance matter.
A decision under actual HR, legal, safety or related authority. A practice course scenario does not adjudicate discipline, threat or fitness.

accordion.heading: Respond with both clarity and care

items.title: Coworker questions
items.body: Explain the operational expectation and respect for privacy. Do not disclose the condition to persuade the team that an arrangement is deserved. If the question reveals a real coverage problem, address that work issue separately.

items.title: Performance questions
items.body: Use the relevant standard and observed facts. A request should not be ignored because performance is already under review, but the request does not automatically decide the earlier issue. Coordinate the processes with the appropriate roles.

items.title: Safety questions
items.body: Distinguish an emergency response from a formal assessment. Do not infer a threat from a condition name, appearance or rumor. Bring actual facts to authorized staff and use immediate procedures when an emergency requires them.

tabs.label: Operational plan
tabs.body: Who handles a shared task and how colleagues coordinate it. Provide what is necessary for work without disclosing a personal reason.

tabs.label: Personal record
tabs.body: Medical and accommodation details belong in the authorized confidential process with applicable access limits. A group chat or supervisor’s informal file is not an appropriate substitute.

tabs.label: Formal case question
tabs.body: A disputed performance, safety or disclosure question needs the actual process and facts. Do not use an instructional example as a verdict on a real employee.

check.question: A coworker asks why an employee has a different arrangement. What is the supervisor’s appropriate response?
check.correct: Explain necessary work coordination and privacy expectations without disclosing confidential medical or accommodation information.
wrong: Share the diagnosis so coworkers agree the arrangement is deserved.
Ask the group to vote on the accommodation.
Assume the question proves the employee’s request was dishonest.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. Work can be coordinated without revealing private reasons. Address a genuine coverage issue separately and leave personal decisions with authorized roles.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Curiosity, a vote or speculation does not create authority to disclose or decide the request. Keep the operational and confidential information distinct.

sorting.heading: Which information or question is this?

items.text: The shared response mailbox will be covered by the assigned team role.
The employee’s medical documentation is reviewed by authorized staff.
The condition label proves the employee is unsafe.
Colleagues use the agreed route for urgent work questions.
An actual denial or disclosure issue needs the authorized review.
A new request automatically erases every past conduct finding.

lessons.next: The final lesson checks implementation, effectiveness and changed circumstances without restarting an unnecessary medical interview.

scenario.context: In this example, a supervisor receives an accommodation request during an existing performance review. They propose either ignoring the request or automatically deleting the earlier review.
options: Keep the actual performance facts in their proper process and handle the prospective accommodation request through the authorized process, with appropriate HR and coordinator guidance.
Ignore every request once a performance concern exists.
Erase all earlier records solely because a request was made.
responses: This preserves both questions without deciding either from an automatic rule. The actual facts, standards and authority matter.
The request can still need prospective consideration. A performance concern does not automatically remove the process.
A request does not by itself determine the treatment of past events or records. Use the proper authority and applicable rules.

lessons.transfer: Write a practice operational explanation that contains no diagnosis, then identify the separate formal question that belongs with HR or the coordinator.

move.control: You can protect privacy while keeping work expectations clear.
move.failure: Medical disclosure or an automatic rule replaces a fair process.
move.next: Separate coordination from confidential information and route actual case decisions appropriately.

lessons.title: Follow through as the task and needs change
lessons.summary: Approval, provision and effectiveness are different. Changed circumstances can require renewed discussion through the proper process.
lessons.objective: Distinguish approval, delivery and effectiveness in a follow-up note.
objectives: Distinguish approval, delivery and effectiveness in a follow-up note.
Plan a focused task check without unnecessary medical inquiry.
Recognize a changed circumstance or delayed implementation that needs further process attention.
takeaways: An approved option still needs appropriate implementation.
Check the relevant task result rather than assuming a purchase worked.
Respond to changed barriers without demanding repeated medical proof yourself.
lessons.statement: Follow-through lets the person describe the current work result without having to defend the original request again.

image.caption: A brief task-focused check can identify a remaining barrier and the right next owner.

intro.heading: Check what is available and what it achieves
intro.body:
The practice DHS analyst’s adjustment is approved, but the new arrangement is not yet in place. A later purchase is delivered, yet it does not work with the required report format. These are different statuses. Approval is evidence of a decision; provision shows an action; effectiveness concerns the actual barrier and work result. A supervisor should not close the process simply because an email or receipt exists.

MMB Policy 1433 calls for prompt provision of approved accommodation and describes status communication when it cannot be provided within a reasonable time. In that circumstance, the decision-maker informs the requester before the end of 30 days; feasible temporary measures can provide assistance. This is not universal permission to wait 30 days or a guarantee that every request has the same completion date. Use the actual policy and responsible process.

Ask a focused work question: can the employee now complete the relevant task, and what remains difficult? The supervisor can listen and bring unresolved effectiveness to the coordinator or technical owner. Do not request medical records yourself or repeat a settled documentation question as a routine follow-up. Appropriate documentation decisions remain with the authorized roles.

Non-apparent and episodic needs may vary, and work conditions also change. A new application, altered duty or different environment can affect an arrangement that once worked. The current regulation recognizes the relevant episodic disability principle, but the course does not diagnose a person or guarantee a particular adjustment. Recognize the changed barrier and return to the process when needed.

Keep records and privacy boundaries accurate. For broader improvement, use appropriate non-identifying lessons about recurring tool failures, delay or unclear referral rather than a list of diagnoses. In the practice exercise, write what was approved, what is available, what was checked and what needs attention. Reliable follow-through supports the work and preserves the person’s dignity without turning every check into a new eligibility debate.

inThisLesson: Check the current task without medical collection.
Revisit changed barriers through the process.
lessons.keyStatement: A receipt or earlier success does not establish current effectiveness.

flashcards.back: The authorized process has decided to provide an adjustment. Delivery and effectiveness may still be pending.
The arrangement or tool is available. Its effect in the actual task still needs appropriate attention.
The arrangement addresses the relevant barrier in the current work circumstances. Record the task result and limits rather than assuming every future situation is settled.
A new or altered condition affects the work. It may need a further exchange through the proper process without a supervisor collecting medical proof.

items.title: Ask about the task result
items.body: Use a concrete question about the duty the arrangement was intended to support. A reported remaining difficulty deserves inquiry, not a judgment about gratitude or sincerity. Bring the relevant facts to the appropriate owner.

items.title: Keep delay visible
items.body: Identify what is pending and who handles the next process update. Follow the policy’s status duties and consider feasible temporary assistance through the proper route. Do not portray one timeline provision as a blanket waiting period.

items.title: Learn without exposing people
items.body: A recurring configuration failure may inform better technical review. Use non-identifying information appropriate to the audience, protect confidential records and investigate before claiming a cause or assigning blame.

tabs.label: Approval email
tabs.body: Shows the authorized decision. It does not prove delivery or that the current task is effective. Ask what followed.

tabs.label: Installed tool
tabs.body: Shows provision of technology in some context. Check the actual agency task and configuration before recording the barrier as resolved.

tabs.label: Current work feedback
tabs.body: Gives useful information about the task result and remaining barrier. It can inform the proper process without requiring the person to supply a medical history to the supervisor.

check.question: A purchased tool is installed but cannot support the employee’s required task. What should the follow-up say?
check.correct: The tool is provided, but effectiveness remains unresolved and needs attention through the appropriate accommodation and support process.
wrong: The request is fully resolved because money was spent.
The employee should be considered ungrateful for reporting a problem.
The supervisor must immediately collect a complete new medical record.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. This states the action and limit accurately. The remaining task barrier needs the responsible response without an unsupported character judgment or improper documentation request.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Spending and installation are not the same as effectiveness. Focus on the actual task and the policy’s roles rather than demanding gratitude or medical proof.

items.text: The authorized response says the adjustment is approved.
The agreed tool is installed on the actual workstation.
Can the analyst now complete the required review?
The coordinator communicates the approved recurring arrangement.
The agreed support is present for the scheduled activity.
A new application changes the task that previously worked.

lessons.next: Use the job aid to prepare a practice response and follow it into the task. Related courses examine the interactive process and supervisor responsibilities in more detail.

scenario.context: In this example, an employee’s arrangement worked until the required software changed. The supervisor says a non-apparent condition should not need further discussion because the original request was approved.
options: Close the concern from the old approval alone.
Recognize the changed task barrier, discuss its work effect and involve the appropriate process while preserving confidentiality.
Ask coworkers to verify whether the condition still looks real.
responses: The previous decision does not establish current effectiveness after a task change.
This responds to the actual circumstances without diagnosing or automatically approving a new option. Appropriate roles handle any documentation or formal decision.
Appearance and coworker opinions do not determine disability or need. Keep the personal process private.

lessons.transfer: Draft a practice follow-up using approval, provision, checked task result and remaining action as four separate statements.

move.control: You can check the real result and keep a route for changed needs.
move.failure: A past decision or purchase becomes permanent proof of effectiveness.
move.next: Listen to current task feedback and return unresolved barriers to the appropriate process.

jobAid.subtitle: A respectful supervisor response to a non-apparent work barrier
remember: Visibility does not establish the presence or absence of a disability.
Recognize requests in ordinary language without requiring public disclosure.
Supervisors do not request accommodation medical documentation under Policy 1433.
Actual eligibility, denial, safety and employment decisions stay in authorized processes.

sections.heading: Notice and acknowledge
items: Describe the work observation and what remains unknown.
Avoid diagnosis, motive judgments and coworker speculation.
Recognize a possible request and explain the real next route promptly.

sections.heading: Prepare the work discussion
items: Identify the actual duty, required result and barrier.
Distinguish a customary method from an essential-function question.
Consider the person’s input and compare options for the task through the proper process.
Keep shared improvements and individual decisions related but distinct.

sections.heading: Protect and follow through
items: Communicate operational arrangements without revealing private medical or accommodation information.
Keep performance, safety and documentation questions in their proper routes.
Respond to changed barriers and learn from appropriate non-identifying patterns.
